reason: The front of the arm has a space for the biceps, and the introduction says to build it from muscle cells.
expectation: The muscle cells should help build the biceps in the front of the arm.

alternatives.reason: The bone attachment also needs mineral, and the introduction says either order works.

effect: The muscle cells built the biceps, but the radius still needs mineral.
reaction: It is satisfying to see how the biceps pulls to bend the elbow.
reason: The front attachment still needs bone mineral, which the result says hardens the bone the tendon pulls on.
expectation: The mineral should strengthen the bone at the biceps attachment.

alternatives.reason: I could build the triceps before finishing the front.

effect: The front attachment is mineralized and its goal is complete; the back of the arm still needs its muscle and bone mineral.
reaction: The distinction between hard bone and the soft tendon is helpful.
reason: The back of the arm has a space for the triceps, which the introduction says is built from muscle cells.
expectation: The muscle cells should build the triceps on the back of the arm.

alternatives.reason: I could strengthen the back attachment first, since either order works.

effect: The triceps is built and straightens the elbow, but its ulna attachment still needs mineral.
reaction: It is interesting that the same kind of muscle cells has a different effect because of where it attaches.
reason: The back attachment still needs bone mineral, just as the front attachment did.
expectation: The mineral should strengthen the bone at the triceps attachment and complete the remaining goal.

effect: The ulna is mineralized, completing the triceps attachment and the chapter.
reaction: The contrast between hard bone and soft tendons was useful, though this repeated the front attachment.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the triceps was most worthwhile: its position behind the elbow explains how the same kind of muscle cells can straighten rather than bend the arm.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding mineral to the back felt repetitive after doing the same thing at the front, even though it completed the other attachment.

surprise.text: I was interested that the same kind of muscle cells can have different effects depending on where the muscles attach.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary: the slots and pictures made the muscle and mineral pairings clear.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, because seeing how the muscles' positions change their effects made me curious about how other body parts work together.
